agent_notes: This diff is a tightening change: it adds SSRF validation (via the already-existing, previously-unused `validate_arr_url_config` helper added in commit 14eecb5) to the config-file load path, which previously had zero SSRF checking (only the apikey-in-URL check `reject_apikey_in_url` ran on config load). It closes a real gap rather than opening one.

Verified the new validator is strictly a subset of what the web-UI save path already enforces: triggarr/web/routes.py:561 calls the stricter `validate_arr_url` (which also blocks loopback) unconditionally on every submitted instance URL, including disabled ones, before the model is even constructed. Any URL ever saved through the app's own settings UI will therefore already satisfy the new, more relaxed `validate_arr_url_config` check — no web-saved config can newly fail to load because of this diff.

The validator intentionally runs unconditionally regardless of `enabled` (per its docstring and the design doc at .planning/phases/71-presentation-rewrite/71-02-PLAN.md, which explicitly specifies this and has a test asserting a disabled instance with a metadata URL still raises). A hand-edited triggarr.toml with a non-conforming URL on a disabled instance would now fail Settings() construction. Per triggarr/config.py:333-373 (`ensure_config`), uncaught `pydantic.ValidationError` is documented and intended to propagate and crash startup ('schema bug... continue to propagate uncaught') — this is consistent with the codebase's existing fail-loud convention for config validation errors (same behavior already applies to the pre-existing apikey-in-URL check and the max-5-instances check), so this is not a new architectural deviation.

Checked validate_arr_url_config's own logic (triggarr/web/validation.py:111-173, unchanged by this diff) for IPv4-mapped IPv6 bypass handling (::ffff:x.y.z.w) — it correctly re-checks the mapped address against link-local/unspecified/multicast/_BLOCKED_NETWORKS. Did not find a concrete bypass in the function itself beyond the already-documented, accepted DNS-hostname/rebinding gap noted in finding sec-001.
No hardcoded secrets, logging of secrets, injection, or auth/authorization issues identified in this diff; the change is confined to one Pydantic field_validator.

findings.problem: The new field_validator wires `validate_arr_url_config` (triggarr/web/validation.py:111) into TOML config-load, extending SSRF checking to a path that previously had none. That helper allows loopback and arbitrary DNS hostnames (including `localhost`) without resolving them, so a hostname that resolves to a blocked address (link-local, metadata IP, etc.) at connection time is not caught by this check — this is the same documented 'DNS rebinding is an accepted residual risk' behavior already present in the sibling `validate_arr_url` function used by the web settings-save path (triggarr/web/routes.py:561), so this diff does not newly create the gap, only reaches it from one more call site.
findings.title: Config-load SSRF validator leaves DNS hostnames unresolved (documented residual risk, no new bypass found)
findings.why_it_matters: If an attacker or misconfiguration could get a hostname like `internal-metadata.example` added to config (pointing at 169.254.169.254 via DNS), outbound *arr requests could reach cloud metadata or internal-only services despite this validator. No concrete bypass path into this specific diff is demonstrated here; this is the same pre-existing, explicitly-accepted limitation of the underlying validator, not a regression introduced by wiring it up. pending: a concrete reachable hostname/attacker-controlled DNS entry that an operator or external actor can inject into `triggarr.toml`'s instance `url` field.

agent_notes: Import cycle check: no cycle. triggarr/web/validation.py imports only ipaddress, re and urllib.parse, and nothing from triggarr. triggarr/web/__init__.py is empty, so importing triggarr.web.validation does not pull in FastAPI routes or the app. The edge models/config.py -> web/validation.py has no path back.

Layering: this diff adds the first import from triggarr/models/ into triggarr/web/. Before it, models/config.py imported only stdlib and pydantic, and the only other non-web modules that reach into web are triggarr/__main__.py and triggarr/search/scheduler.py (scheduler.py:532 and :538, both function-local imports of triggarr.web.routes). Having the domain-model layer depend on the web package is an inverted dependency. However, .planning/phases/71-presentation-rewrite/71-02-PLAN.md explicitly authorizes this exact edge: 'from: triggarr/models/config.py InstanceConfig.url / to: triggarr.web.validation.validate_arr_url_config / via: field_validator local import + call, raising ValueError'. Under the SAFE rule it is not reported as a finding. A cleaner home later would be a layer-neutral module (for example triggarr/url_safety.py) imported by both web/validation.py and models/config.py.

The function-local import is not needed: the plan's reason ('module-level import would risk a circular import') does not apply, as the same plan admits ('web.validation imports nothing from models'). The cost is small: one sys.modules lookup per InstanceConfig construction, plus the dependency is hidden from top-of-file import scanners. A module-level import would work today. Not reported as a finding because the plan requires it ('The new validator uses a local (in-function) import') and it is harmless.

Duplication: validate_arr_url_config (web/validation.py:111, from the earlier commit 14eecb5, not in this diff) copies about 90% of validate_arr_url (web/validation.py:56), differing only in whether loopback is checked. That makes two copies, below the rule-of-three threshold, so no finding. If a third variant appears, parameterize one function (for example allow_loopback: bool) so the BLOCKED_HOSTS and IPv4-mapped-IPv6 logic cannot drift between copies.

Pattern consistency: the new validator follows the existing reject_apikey_in_url pattern: @field_validator('url') + @classmethod, raising ValueError so Pydantic surfaces a ValidationError. Pydantic v2 runs same-field validators in definition order, so the apikey check runs first, which the plan requires and its tests cover (71-02-PLAN.md:181).

Two URL policies now exist: strict in the web form (routes.py:561 uses validate_arr_url, which blocks loopback) and relaxed at config load (blocks only metadata, link-local, unspecified and multicast). This is deliberate per D-02/D-03. Product-visible effect: a URL like http://127.0.0.1:7878 loads from triggarr.toml but cannot be saved through the settings UI. Also, a saved config passes through both validators, since the form check runs first and then InstanceConfig construction, so an existing loopback URL may round-trip oddly if the form re-submits it unchanged. Pending: whether routes.py re-validates URLs it did not change on save is out of scope here; it belongs to the impact/bugs agents.

Startup blast radius: InstanceConfig is imported by 15 production modules and about 20 test files. The validator runs on every construction, including for disabled instances, so an existing triggarr.toml with a link-local or metadata URL on a disabled instance will now fail at startup. The plan documents this as intended hardening (71-02-PLAN.md:19 and :180). Noted for the impact agent, not an architectural defect.

agent_notes: Change: adds a second field validator on InstanceConfig.url that calls the new relaxed validator validate_arr_url_config (triggarr/web/validation.py:111). This tightens validation and adds no new path for input to get through.

Blast radius: InstanceConfig is imported by about 15 production modules and about 20 test files. It is built at startup through ensure_config -> load_settings (startup.py:192), in the settings POST (routes.py:598), in add-instance (routes.py:790, default url='' which passes the empty-string early return), and through load_settings reloads after setup, security and API-key changes (routes.py:1199, ~1462, ~1511, ~1535). The reloads re-read files the app wrote from already-validated settings, so they cannot newly fail unless the TOML was hand-edited between writes.

Public API and signatures: unchanged. The model's fields, defaults and serialization are the same. The only behavior change is that construction can now raise for a URL that is not http(s), has no hostname, is a known metadata host, or is a link-local, unspecified or multicast IP literal.

Newly rejected values compared with before: `0.0.0.0` and `[::]` (unspecified addresses), 169.254.x.x, IPv4-mapped forms of these and of 100.64.0.0/10, and scheme-less strings like `radarr:7878`. Loopback and plain 100.x (Tailscale CGNAT) IPv4 literals are still allowed, since _BLOCKED_NETWORKS is only checked for IPv4-mapped IPv6 addresses; only the exact 100.100.100.200 is blocked through BLOCKED_HOSTS. Ordinary Tailscale node IPs are not affected.
Ordering: reject_apikey_in_url (config.py:65) is defined first and runs first. If it raises, the SSRF validator does not run, so the error message is the apikey one. No conflict.

Error exposure: the ValidationError text includes input_value, which is the URL. At startup it propagates as a traceback, and in the settings POST it is logged at routes.py:600. URLs carrying an apikey are already rejected by the earlier validator, so API-key exposure through this path is not a new risk.
Database, schema and migration: none. The TOML layout is unchanged, and no state or db migration is needed.
Performance: negligible. The function-local import resolves from sys.modules after the first call, and the validator runs only on config construction, not per request.
Cross-process: single daemon; no multi-instance coordination concerns.

Verdict: shippable as-is. The only notable effect is fail-fast startup with a raw traceback for hand-edited TOML outside the documented URL contract. Consider a friendly ValidationError handler in ensure_config, and aligning the form validator (routes.py:561) with the relaxed loader.
